summary: IPv6 privacy address rotation breaks WireGuard peer rekey and SSH sessions
description:
Issue summary: Several engineers reported losing long-lived SSH sessions to internal hosts after laptops moved between access points or after system suspend/resume. Root cause appears to be IPv6 temporary (privacy) address rotation causing the endpoint observed by the WireGuard peer to change, triggering a rekey and leaving in-flight TCP sessions (SSH) stalled until a manual restart of the VPN interface or agent.

Impact: Intermittent session drops for ~10-20% of laptop handoffs and after suspend/resume. Affects internal engineering teams in SF office on corporate Wi‑Fi using the zero-trust WireGuard client. Not customer-facing but high productivity impact for on-site devs.

Observed behavior: On move/suspend event the laptop obtains a new IPv6 privacy address. WireGuard peer sees endpoint change and performs handshake/rekey. Some existing TCP connections are not NAT-translated correctly by the office AP/NAT path during the transition, causing SSH connections to hang (no packet flow). "Restart wg" or disabling IPv6 temporary address on the host restores connectivity.

Expected behavior: WireGuard rekey should be seamless and preserve TCP sessions or zero-trust agent should gracefully migrate NAT mappings so SSH and other long-lived connections survive address rotation.

Additional context: Several ticketed occurrences correlate to AP handoffs within the same SSID (fast BSS transition) and to kernel privacy address regeneration events (net.ipv6.conf.*.use_tempaddr).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Boot laptop and connect to corporate Wi‑Fi (office sf).
2) Establish long-lived SSH session to internal bastion (ssh -T -o TCPKeepAlive=yes).
3) Trigger suspend/resume or force AP roam (move between desks/rooms).
4) Observe that laptop acquires a new IPv6 temporary address (ip -6 addr show).
5) Observe WireGuard rekey/handshake on the server side (wg show / journalctl -u wg-quick).
6) Verify that SSH stalls and packets are not forwarded until wg-quick restart or zero-trust-agent restart.
logs: Client: ip -6 addr show dev wlp3s0 -> inet6 2601:XXXX:YYYY:ABCD:ZZZZ:ZZZZ:ZZZZ:1234/64 scope global temporary dynamic
Server: wg show peer <peer-key> endpoint 2601:XXXX:YYYY:ABCD:ZZZZ:ZZZZ:ZZZZ:5678:51820 latest-handshake: 24s ago
journalctl -u zero-trust-agent: Mar 11 09:12:04 kernel: ipv6: duplicate address detected, veering?
tcpdump on AP: no TCP packets from old client IPv6 when endpoint changes (only ICMPv6 RA/NS seen)
ssh client stuck: application shows stall but connection not reset (no TCP RST observed)
wg show conf: persistent-keepalive = 25s on client, handshake initiated but NAT binding timed out on path.
investigation_notes: Confirmed privacy address rotation coincident with suspend/resume and with network roam events using tcpdump and ip -6 addr history.

WireGuard triggers a handshake when endpoint changes; handshake succeeds but the NAT/flow state on the AP and edge NAT sometimes does not translate ephemeral old TCP state to new source address quickly enough.
Observed that disabling temporary addresses (sysctl net.ipv6.conf.all.use_tempaddr=0) prevents the problem but is not acceptable as a permanent policy due to privacy requirements on managed devices.

Hypothesis: AP/edge NAT implementation drops existing TCP conntrack entries when it sees a new source IPv6 address from the same MAC/4-tuple; the zero-trust-agent/wg-client does a rekey which new packets arrive on different source address before NAT has remapped flows.
Reproduced against a lab AP (same vendor) and confirmed gap ~2-15s between handshake completion and application-level recovery leading to hung SSH sessions.
Checked kernel logs for RFC 4941 rotation triggers and verified rotation interval is default (hourly) but rotation also occurs at link events and resume which explains higher incidence.
comments: Morgan Li (reporter) -- 2026-03-10: Noticed multiple engineers lose SSH after coming back from lunch or moving floors. Restarting the VPN client fixes immediately.
Diego Ramos (assignee) -- 2026-03-10: Collected tcpdump and wg show from affected laptop and office AP. Early suspicion: IPv6 privacy rotation + AP NAT behavior.
DevOps (SRE) -- 2026-03-11: Reproduced in lab with controlled roam. Need to know AP vendor/model to test NAT behavior across firmware.
Network Eng (Aisha Khan) -- 2026-03-11: SF office uses Aruba APs with controller-managed NAT; opening ticket with Aruba to confirm NAT/conntrack behavior on IPv6 source change.

Diego Ramos -- 2026-03-12: Temporary mitigation deployed to cohort of volunteer laptops: configure systemd-networkd drop-in to set net.ipv6.conf.*.use_tempaddr = 2 (prefer stable with temporary allowed). Monitoring for side effects.
resolution:
Mitigation: Configured a managed profile that sets net.ipv6.conf.<ifaces>.use_tempaddr=2 on enrolled corporate devices to prefer a stable IPv6 address while still allowing temporary addresses as fallback. In parallel, increased WireGuard persistent-keepalive to 45s for volunteers to reduce rekey frequency.

Long-term fix: Tracking two parallel workstreams: 1) Engage with networking vendor (Aruba) to adjust AP/edge NAT conntrack behavior on IPv6 source changes and to evaluate firmware that preserves TCP flows during address migration; 2) Update zero-trust agent to implement a graceful migration mode that maintains NAT mappings by sending a short-burst of translated traffic and re-issuing TCP keepalive-like packets on address change to reestablish conntrack state.

Follow-ups: Create a hardware compatibility note in internal KB, add a sysctl profile for managed devices, and push an engineering task to add graceful-migration support in the zero-trust agent.
